#R2
Define the function box_hist which takes a numeric vector as its only argument and randomly plots either a boxplot or a histogram of the vector.
```{r}
box_hist <- function(n){
  pplot <- rbinom(1, 1, .5)
  
  if (any %in% !as.numeric(n)){ ### checking for any non numerics in vector
    if (pplot == 1 ){
    plot(n)
  } else{
    hist(n)
  }
  }
  else{
    warning("input n is non-numeric!")
  }
}
box_hist(c(4,5,6,6,7))
```
#R3

The Netherlands’ head meteorologist wants to throw a birthday party tomorrow, so she asks one of her employees about the weather she can expect. The code below describes possible outcomes but there is one logical mistake in the code. Try out different scenarios (i.e., weather values) to find, comment, and fix the problem. (Tip: This has nothing to do with salary fairness.)

```{r}
predicted <- "rain"
actual <- "rain"
employee_salary <- 54000

if (actual == "sun"){
    print("Yay! Birthday moved outside!")
    employee_salary <- employee_salary + 500
  } else if (predicted != actual) {
    employee_salary <- employee_salary - 500
  } else if (predicted == actual) {
    employee_salary <- employee_salary + 500
  } else if (actual == "high wind") {
    print("Boss blew off her bike into a canal.")
    employee_salary <- employee_salary
  }
```

#R7
Write two for loops. The first loop should iterate over the columns of the dataframe retrieved above (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hannesrosenbusch/schiphol_class/master/Kaggle_Dataset_Mental_Disorders.csv) and print out the datatype of the current variable. It should skip the variable Sexual.Activity by saying: Private information.

The second for loop should iterate over the rows of the dataframe and print the Patient.Number along with the string “assessed successfully”. When you encounter a patient with NO Authority Respect and signs of Aggressive Response, print “Assessment postponed” and exit the for loop immediately.
```{r}
#Loop 1
patients<- data.frame(read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hannesrosenbusch/schiphol_class/master/Kaggle_Dataset_Mental_Disorders.csv"))
for (i in colnames(patients)){
  if(i == "Sexual.Activity"){
    print("Private Information")
    next()
  }
  print(class(i))
}

#Loop 2
for (i in 1:nrow(patients)){
  if(patients$Authority.Respect[i] == "NO" & patients$Aggressive.Response[i] == "YES"){
    print(patients$Patient.Number[i])
    print("Assessment Postponed")
    break
  }
  print(patients$Patient.Number[i])
  print("Assessed Successfully")
}

```

#R8
The Earth is becoming overpopulated. Currently, world leaders are discussing whether to euthanize everyone with a CO2 footprint of >120. Use a (nested) loop to simulate the CO2 footprints of a city that has exactly 1000 people left AFTER the mass sacrifices (i.e., your data should consist of 1000 CO2 footprint values). For this task, you can assume that CO2 footprints before the sacrifices were normally distributed with a mean of 100 and a standard deviation of 15. Plot your city’s 1000 footprint values in a ggplot2 histogram like this one:
```{r}
library(ggplot2)

survivors<- c()

while (length(survivors) < 1000) {
   co_person<- rnorm(1, 100, 15)
   if (co_person <= 120){
     survivors <- c(survivors, co_person)
   }
}
  print(survivors)
  
survive_df <- data.frame(survivors)
?ggplot2
ggplot(survive_df, mapping = aes(x = survivors)) +
  geom_histogram()
  
```

#R13
The code below simulates a Verhulst equation that describes the growth of rabbits over time (where the variable rabbits represents 1000 rabbits). Observe that in the code above we created our own function in one line. We can also create a for loop in one line. Notice the confusing lack of curly brackets. Rewrite the function and for loop so that they both have multiple lines with indentations and brackets.

```{r}
verhulst <- function(x, rate_in, cap) rate_in*x*(cap-x)/cap
rabbits <- c(.001)
rate <- 2
capacity <- 1000
for (time in 2:50) rabbits[time] <- verhulst(rabbits[time-1], rate, capacity)
plot(rabbits, type='l', xlab='time', bty='n')
```

#R19
a) write a function called assess_patient that accepts a numerical vector of seven mood ratings. call the argumnet week_ratings
b) if input is not a vector with seven elements, the function should raise that error 
c) if vector is not numeric, function should raise a warning that "input is not numeric" and attempt to coerce the input to numeric
d) function should return your professional judgement about how the patient is doings. use at least two conditions 

```{r}
assess_patient <- function(week_ratings){
  
  ##if not in 7
  if(length(week_ratings) != 7 ){
    stop("error!")
   ## geterrmessage()
  }
  if(!is.numeric(week_ratings)){
    warning("Input is not numeric!")
    week_ratings <- as.numeric(week_ratings)
  }
  ##Patient assessment
  if(mean(rm.na(week_ratings)) < 10 && rm.na(min(week_ratings)) < 5){
    return("Patient should have followup session.")
  } else{
    return("Patient is well.")
  }
  
  return(week_ratings)
}


patient <- c("lol",4,3,4,5, 8, 9)
assess_patient(patient)

```
